title: The brain bot
bridge: The brain bot is like Nova's Slack app from g3-13. It is a Bolt app in Socket Mode that dials out to Slack, so it needs no public URL. Except: it is written in Python, not TypeScript, because it imports Shai's kb_tools in-process. So it ranks pages and redacts exactly like the kb CLI and BRAIN-QA.
intro: Most questions are asked in Slack, not in Claude Code. This lesson builds a small bot that answers @Rhino Brain mentions in allow-listed public channels. It answers with citations, or says it does not know. Then we deploy it on inf-rhinohealth like n8n, and harden it. Hard questions fan out to read-only helpers, and a checker confirms each claim. A thumbs-down opens an issue for the page owner.

picture.caption: The model reads mirrors and returns structured JSON; our code checks the citations and posts the reply.

p: The agent platform is TypeScript on Node 24 (ts_platform.md). The brain bot is the one agent service that stays Python, and the reason is in the ticket: it imports kb_tools in-process. kb_tools holds the stdlib search ranking and the PHI scan. The kb CLI, BRAIN-QA and the bot must rank pages and redact the same way, so all three import the same module. Shai and Nave own that repo's language.

So the bot uses Bolt for Python and the Python Agent SDK (claude_agent_sdk). The shape is the same as Nova's Slack app: Socket Mode, no public endpoint, the gateway adds the key. Only the language differs.

The file has three parts: the options for the agent session, an answer() function, and the Slack handler. The options are the walls in code. Read-only tools only, no setting sources and a system prompt from a file. And a JSON schema for the output, so our code can check the citations.
The model is Sonnet 5.5 at low effort, with a prompt line to search even when confident. ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is the LLM gateway, which adds the brain-bot key.
sections.because: We ask for structured output with a citations list, because our code can only check what it can parse. A citation inside free text cannot be checked.

code.text:
# rnd-kb-tooling/bot/app.py: sketch. Runs on inf-rhinohealth; ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is the LLM gateway (it adds the key).
import asyncio
import os

from claude_agent_sdk import ClaudeAgentOptions, ResultMessage, query
from slack_bolt.adapter.socket_mode.async_handler import AsyncSocketModeHandler
from slack_bolt.async_app import AsyncApp

from bot.citations import ANSWER, format_reply, keep_resolvable  # ANSWER: {answer, citations, unverified} schema
from kb_tools.scan import has_blocked_terms, redact  # same PHI patterns and deny-list as kb-lint

app = AsyncApp(token=os.environ["SLACK_BOT_TOKEN"])
CHANNELS = set(os.environ["BRAIN_CHANNELS"].split(","))  # public engineering channels only (DATA-SCOPE.md)
OPTIONS = ClaudeAgentOptions(
    model="claude-sonnet-5-5", effort="low",
    cwd="/mirror/rnd-kb", add_dirs=["/mirror/fcp"],  # read-only git mirrors, refreshed every 10 minutes
    tools=["Read", "Grep", "Glob"], setting_sources=[],  # no Bash, no writes, no web, no local config
    system_prompt=open("/app/prompts/brain.md").read(),
    output_format={"type": "json_schema", "schema": ANSWER})

notes.text: Runs on inf-rhinohealth; the gateway URL is the only model endpoint it knows.
The Python Agent SDK: options, the result message type, and query().
Bolt's async Socket Mode handler: the bot dials out to Slack over a websocket.
ANSWER is the JSON schema {answer, citations, unverified}; keep_resolvable and format_reply are our own code.
has_blocked_terms and redact come from kb_tools.scan: the same PHI patterns and deny-list as kb-lint.
The Bolt app with the bot token from the environment (Vault writes it into the pod).
BRAIN_CHANNELS: the public engineering channels from G6-01; the bot answers nowhere else.
Sonnet 5.5 at low effort: enough for a cited answer from one page.
cwd is the rnd-kb mirror; add_dirs adds the fcp mirror. Both are read-only git mirrors refreshed every 10 minutes.
Read, Grep and Glob only, and no setting sources: no Bash, no writes, no web, no local config. Check the docs for the exact option name in the pinned Python SDK (tools vs allowed_tools).
output_format with the ANSWER schema: the result arrives as JSON we can check.

p: answer() runs one query and returns the structured output. Before that, keep_resolvable() drops every citation that does not resolve to a file in the mirror at its sha. With none left, the reply becomes "I don't know" and where to ask.
The handler checks the channel and the text before any model call, and posts the reply itself after redacting deny-list terms. The model never calls Slack.
sections.because: We check channel and text before the model call, because a refused question should cost nothing and leak nothing.

notes.text: answer() is async: Bolt's async app and the SDK's async iterator fit together.
query() yields messages as the session runs; we wait for the final one.
ResultMessage carries structured_output when a schema was given.
keep_resolvable drops citations missing at the mirror's sha and turns an empty list into 'I don't know'.
app_mention fires only when someone writes @Rhino Brain.
Wall 1: not an allowed channel, or the text has PHI-like or deny-list terms: refuse with one fixed sentence.
Reply in the thread (thread_ts) with the formatted, redacted answer.
Start the Socket Mode handler with the app-level token. No HTTP server, no public route.

sections.ifInstead: If instead the bot replies to a mention in a channel you did not list, BRAIN_CHANNELS is wrong or empty. The check is on channel IDs (C0123...), not names.

p: Inf tools are Terraform helm_release units in the infrastructure repo, not Argo apps (lesson p5-2). The bot follows the n8n pattern. A new ECR repo rnd-kb-bot with immutable tags, and a secrets unit that owns the Vault path infrastructure/brain-bot. Then a repository unit that deploys the chart. A person writes the Slack bot and app tokens, the rhino-kb App key and the read-only Jira token into Vault.

The repository unit uses the generic agent-services module from G3 (its final name is not decided; the sketch calls it ai-agents-service). One replica, because Socket Mode holds one connection. No Service and no HTTPRoute, because the bot dials out. A NetworkPolicy allows egress only to Slack, GitHub, the Jira site and the gateway service.
sections.because: We reuse the agent-services module instead of writing a second one. Every agent service on inf should deploy the same way and be reviewed once.

notes.text: include root: the old multi_tenant tree's root.hcl, like n8n's units.
brain-bot.hcl next to the units holds the shared locals: namespace, image digest, gateway URL, channels.
The comment records the open point: the module's name comes from G3's deploy ticket.
source points at the module folder; the trailing // marks the module root for Terragrunt.
dependency secrets: this unit reads the Vault path from the secrets unit's outputs.
mock_outputs let terragrunt validate and plan run before the secrets unit is applied.

sections.h: The inputs: image, secrets, env, mirrors
p: The inputs block is what a reviewer reads. Image by digest, one replica, the Vault path and no exposure. Then the two environment variables the code reads, and the two git mirrors the code expects at /mirror/.
The plan is run locally over VPN and pasted into the PR, as today; a person applies. An alert goes to #ai-agents-alerts when the pod restarts more than 3 times in an hour.
sections.because: We pin the image by digest because a tag can move and a digest cannot. So the running bot is exactly the one that passed CI.

notes.text: name brain-bot; the pod, the ExternalSecret and the NetworkPolicy take this name.
namespace ai-agents: next to the broker, the gateway and the Slack app.
The ECR image in the inf account, by digest from brain-bot.hcl.
replicas 1: one Socket Mode connection.
vault_secret_path from the secrets unit: the ExternalSecret reads this path from vault-store.
expose false: no Service, no HTTPRoute.
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: the gateway. The pod never holds an Anthropic key.
BRAIN_CHANNELS joined from the list in brain-bot.hcl.
git_mirrors: the module runs a git-sync sidecar per entry, read-only, every 10 minutes.

callout.text: Agents never apply. The plan is posted; a person applies. The bot's pod holds Slack and GitHub tokens from Vault. It has no Anthropic key, and no write access to any repo except issues on rnd-kb.

sections.h: Hard questions: fan out and check (G6-23)
p: Simple questions need one page. Hard ones span code and tickets, where one pass guesses. So a router (Haiku 5.5 at low effort, structured output) labels each question simple or hard. Simple stays on v0.

Hard runs Sonnet 5.5 at high effort with the Agent tool and read-only helpers (lesson p8-5). code-reader, kb-reader and jira-reader return pointers. A checker re-reads each cited source and keeps a claim only if the source says it. Unchecked claims are listed under "unverified", never dropped silently.
jira-reader needs Jira. We give it an in-process, read-only jira_search tool; the token comes from Vault and never enters a prompt.
sections.because: We define the Jira tool in our own code. Then the model may search tickets without ever seeing a token or a write method.

notes.text: AgentDefinition describes a helper; create_sdk_mcp_server and tool make an in-process tool server.
search_issues: our read-only Jira client with the Vault token.
@tool declares the tool: name, description (what the model reads) and the input shape {jql: str}.
The handler runs the JQL and returns up to 20 results as text.
helper() builds an AgentDefinition from a description, a prompt file, a tools list, a model and an effort.

p: HELPERS maps a name to its definition. Three readers on Haiku 5.5 at medium return pointers (file:line or path@sha). The checker on Sonnet 5.5 at medium re-reads each cited source. hard_options() takes the v0 options and adds effort high, the Agent tool, the helpers and the Jira server. Helpers cannot start helpers.

The thumbs-down: on reaction_added with name -1 on a bot reply, the bot opens an issue in rnd-kb. The issue holds the question, the answer and the cited pages. It is assigned to the owner from OWNERS.yml, through the rhino-kb App with issues:write. Public channels only, so the text can be verbatim.
Ten hard questions join BRAIN-QA's nightly run. The fan-out stays only if correctness goes up, and cost per answer is watched in Grafana.
sections.because: We send a thumbs-down to the page owner as an issue. A bad answer usually means a page is wrong or missing, and the owner is the one who can fix that.

code.text:
HELPERS = {
    "code-reader": helper("Finds where something happens in fcp; returns file:line pointers.", "code_reader.md",
                          ["Read", "Grep", "Glob"], "claude-haiku-5-5", "medium"),
    "kb-reader": helper("Finds brain pages that cover the question; returns path@sha.", "kb_reader.md",
                        ["Read", "Grep", "Glob"], "claude-haiku-5-5", "medium"),
    "jira-reader": helper("Finds tickets and epics that explain a change or a decision.", "jira_reader.md",
                          ["mcp__jira__jira_search"], "claude-haiku-5-5", "medium"),
    "checker": helper("Re-reads each cited source and keeps only claims the source supports.", "checker.md",
                      ["Read", "Grep", "mcp__jira__jira_search"], "claude-sonnet-5-5", "medium"),
}


def hard_options(base: ClaudeAgentOptions) -> ClaudeAgentOptions:
    base.effort = "high"
    base.tools = ["Read", "Grep", "Glob", "Agent"]  # still read-only; helpers can't start helpers
    base.agents = HELPERS
    base.mcp_servers = {"jira": create_sdk_mcp_server(name="jira", version="1.0.0", tools=[jira_search])}
    return base

notes.text: HELPERS: name to AgentDefinition. The model picks a helper by its description.
code-reader: Read, Grep, Glob over the fcp mirror; Haiku 5.5 at medium; returns file:line.
kb-reader: the same tools over the rnd-kb mirror; returns path@sha.
jira-reader: only the mcp__jira__jira_search tool; nothing else.
checker: Sonnet 5.5 at medium, with Read, Grep and the Jira tool, keeps only supported claims.
hard_options() starts from the v0 options and raises effort to high.
The main session gets Read, Grep, Glob and Agent. Still read-only; helpers cannot start helpers.
The in-process MCP server named jira exposes jira_search to the helpers that list it.

lab.faded: Add has_blocked_terms(text) with a small deny-list and one PHI-like pattern (a 9-digit number). Add a test that the on_mention path would refuse 'patient 123456789 in Acme hospital' before any model call. Write the regular expression yourself.
lab.alone: Write hard_router.py: a function route(question) that returns 'simple' or 'hard' without a model. Use two rules you choose, for example: mentions a ticket key or two areas means hard. Add five tests. Then write, in a comment, which questions a real Haiku router would get right that your rules miss.
lab.done: All tests pass, and a citation to a page that is not in the mirror becomes an 'I don't know' reply. Blocked text is refused before a model call.

quiz.q: The model returns a citation to rnd-kb/engineering/old-page.md@<current sha>, but that file was deleted last week. What happens?

options.text: The reply shows it; the sha matches, so it is valid.
options.why: keep_resolvable checks that the file exists in the mirror at that sha; a deleted page does not.

options.text: keep_resolvable drops it; with no citations left the bot replies 'I don't know' and where to ask.
options.why: That is the rule in G6-21: every citation must resolve to a file in the mirror at its sha.

options.text: The bot opens an issue for the page owner.
options.why: Issues come from a thumbs-down (G6-23), not from a dropped citation.

quiz.q: Why is the brain bot Python when the rest of the platform is TypeScript?

options.why: Nova's Slack app uses Bolt 5 for TypeScript.

options.text: It imports kb_tools in-process, so it ranks pages and redacts exactly like the kb CLI and BRAIN-QA.
options.why: That is the reason in G6-21 and in ts_platform.md's 'what stays Python' table.

options.text: The Agent SDK's structured output only works in Python.
options.why: Both SDKs support it; the TypeScript option is outputFormat.

quiz.q: Where does the bot get its Anthropic key?

options.text: From Vault, through the ExternalSecret like the Slack tokens.
options.why: The pod holds no Anthropic key; only Slack, GitHub App and Jira tokens come from Vault.

options.text: It has none; ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points at the LLM gateway, which adds the brain-bot key.
options.why: G6-21 and G6-22: the gateway adds the key and meters spend.
Managed settings configure laptops; the bot is a pod on inf.

words.plain: A Slack connection where the app dials out over a websocket, so it needs no public endpoint.
Asking the model to answer in JSON that matches a schema, so code can check the fields.
A read-only clone of a repo kept fresh by a sidecar (git-sync every 10 minutes) that the bot reads from.
A smaller agent with its own tools and model that the main session starts for one job and that returns pointers.
The helper that re-reads each cited source and keeps a claim only if the source supports it.
A Terragrunt folder in the infrastructure repo that deploys a Helm chart; how inf tools like n8n and the bot ship.
